answer: A single ripple checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 264 aliases therefore costs 184 bonds held for 15 days each, plus the terrace attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so a hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a lantern, before it can post or attest. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
